summary: Unexpected streaming connection interruption mid-response after worker eviction/autoscale
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports streaming chat sessions (SSE and websocket flavors) abruptly stop producing tokens mid-response during periods of increased load and concurrent autoscaling activity. Impact: Ongoing user-visible interruptions for AtlasSearch's chat product resulting in degraded UX and several failed transactions. Environment: production cluster in us-west running Dedicated capacity pool 'atlas-dedicated-1' with mixed quantized and float worker fleet.

Observed behavior: Streaming response begins normally, several token chunks stream to the client, then the connection stops emitting further data without a final '[DONE]' frame or explicit HTTP error. Client-side shows persistent TCP connection but no bytes for 8-30 seconds; some clients see immediate connection close. This happens across both SSE and WebSocket endpoints.

Expected behavior: Continuous token stream until completion with explicit end-of-stream marker or proper error code and retry guidance.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use AtlasSearch production account with workload profile that submits 20 concurrent streaming chat requests to /v1/chat/stream with long expected outputs (~800-1200 tokens).
2) Trigger a synthetic load spike (locally or via k6) to raise total per-node concurrency beyond target autoscale threshold to force autoscaler actions.

3) Observe token streaming for ~10-40 tokens and then notice abrupt stop of further tokens; SSE clients show no '[DONE]' and some WebSocket clients report zero-byte frames or immediate connection close.
4) Check server-side logs for worker eviction, preemption, or graceful drain messages around the same timeframe.
logs: 2026-03-12T15:03:22Z INFO serving-runtime: start generation req_id=at-9832 model=llama-2-13b-chat worker=quant-node-7
2026-03-12T15:03:33Z WARN autoscaler: mark_for_eviction worker=quant-node-7 reason=scale_down concurrent_streams=0 cpu=18%
2026-03-12T15:03:34Z INFO scheduler: preempt_notify worker=quant-node-7 draining_sessions=1 req_id=at-9832
comments: 2026-03-12T16:02:11Z - Maya Chen (Support): Customer reported ~12 distinct user sessions observing mid-token stop; attached client pcap and browser console logs. Requests use chunked SSE and a 60s client-side timeout.

2026-03-12T16:45:07Z - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Initial triage shows worker preemption events aligned with timestamps. Opening investigation to check graceful drain path for streaming sessions during eviction.

2026-03-12T18:10:34Z - Nia Patel (Platform): Observed a spike in scheduling latency at 15:03 correlating with rollout of a new quantized worker image in the pool. Possible noisy rollout + autoscaler interplay.

2026-03-13T09:22:50Z - AtlasSearch Ops (Customer): We captured browser console stack: 'EventSource received no further events' and server-sent frames end abruptly; reproduction stable when we disable autoscale policy to keep capacity pinned.

2026-03-13T12:01:03Z - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Added temporary mitigation: increased drain timeout to 60s and forced draining workers to finish in-flight streaming sessions before eviction. Need to validate impact metrics overnight.
2026-03-14T10:45:12Z - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed fewer interruptions after mitigation but still sees sporadic occurrences under higher concurrency (peak at 400 concurrent streams).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Worker eviction preemption race — when the autoscaler marks a worker for shutdown there is a small window where in-flight streaming sessions are not fully flushed; partial flush sends last buffer but connection remains open and gateway closes TCP due to abrupt upstream reset.

Hypothesis B: API gateway/proxy connection reuse bug — proxy reused connections and rotated keepalives causing intermediate silence; downstream client sees no more SSE frames even though server-side generation may resume on a different worker.

Telemetry evidence: Correlation matrix shows 83% of reported incidents occurred within 2s of a worker eviction or worker image rollout in the dedicated pool. CPU and GPU metrics did not show OOM or hard preemption.
Repro attempt: Local load test with a 2s drain delay reproduced truncated streams 4/10 runs when autoscaler triggered scale-down. Increasing drain to 60s reduced reproduction to 1/10.

PRs/links: Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C04SUPPORT/p1647891234000; Playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Streaming+Drain+Guidelines; Related CI PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5247
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-12 18:15Z): Increased worker drain timeout from 10s to 60s in dedicated pools and disabled the rolling image rollout for quantized workers in atlas-dedicated-1. Customer notified and asked to monitor.

Fix plan: 1) Implement graceful-streaming-drain hook to keep SSE/WebSocket session socket pinned until generation completes or configured per-request soft timeout. 2) Make autoscaler respect 'active_streams' metric and avoid evicting nodes with >0 active long-lived streaming sessions. 3) Add end-to-end test for autoscale + streaming behavior in infra CI.

Rollout notes: Change will be staged in prod-US-west for two weeks, then applied globally. Required follow-ups: create runbook entry, add metric alert for post-drain truncated-stream ratio, schedule postmortem if customer sees >1% failure rate during window.
Customer follow-up: AtlasSearch agreed to keep an observational window open for 72 hours and will escalate if issues continue. Support to provide weekly update until fully resolved.
